To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RBE1 and the upstream RBE3 elements both bind the same RBF-2 complex, both are necessary for optimal HIV-1 transcription, and both elements are required for maximal viral expression in infected cells.
the RBE3 and RBE1 elements are both RBF-2 (USF1/2 and TFII-I) binding sites, and mutations in these elements decrease HIV-1 transcription and viral production.
the HIV-1 core promoter contains a second binding site for the USF/TF II-I/RBF-2 complex, and that this site is required for proper viral transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that regulate transcription from the HIV LTR.
the identification and functional characterization of the second RBF- 2 binding site within HIV-1 promoter, and the elucidation of its role in HIV- 1 transcriptional regulation.
the transcription factor binding sites of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1), which is the causative agent of AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RBE1 and 3 are both RBF-2 (USF/TFII- I) binding sites and that both sites are necessary for optimal HIV-1 transcription and viral replication.
both the RBE1 (core promoter) and RBE3 (upstream promoter) elements are required for proper HIV-1 transcription.

the RBE3/RBE1 elements are necessary and sufficient for the binding of USF1, US2, and TF2-I to the HIV-1 5' LTR, and that the presence of the RBE3 and RBE1 elements is required for optimal transcriptional regulation of the HIV-1 gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RBF-2 is a critical transcription factor for HIV-1, and that RBE1 and 3 are both required for RBF-2 function.
RBE3 and RBE1 are both necessary for HIV-1 expression.
the RBF-1 and RBF-2 complexes, through the binding to the RBE1, RBE2, and RBE3 motifs in the HIV-1 U3 region, play a critical role in the transcriptional regulation of HIV-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RBF-1 and RBF-2 complexes are important regulators of HIV- 1 transcription.
RBE3 and RBE1 are functionally redundant and that the RBF-1 transcription factor complex plays a critical role in regulating transcription from the HIV promoter.
the HIV-1 genome contains two binding sites for the RBF transcription factor complex, RBF-2, and that both sites play important roles in HIV-1 transcription.
